g.text: An operator describes an event in their own words.
The service turns the description into an evaluation
plan, runs the plan over each new clip, and stores a
verdict with the frames that support it.
Operators review long stretches of video to find a few events.
A rule written as code needs an engineer for every change.
A reviewer watches hours of footage to confirm a few seconds of it.
A verdict without its frames cannot be checked a month later.
A model update can quietly change what a trigger means.
The operator writes the event; the
service plans it, runs it on every clip, and
keeps the frames that decide it.
Each trigger compiles to an evaluation plan
with a version. A verdict records that version, so a changed plan
shows in the history and is never applied silently.
The API returns once a job is
queued, and a slow clip never holds an operator request open.
YOUR ATTENTION GOES HERE, AND ONLY HERE
You confirm each new or changed plan
A verdict you mark wrong comes
back with its frames and plan version.
every active trigger and waits for your approval.
work moves, in the colour of the actor that sends it
reads or writes the verdict store
one trigger, from description to stored verdict
a lane for each actor; time runs left to right
the pieces, and why each exists
one request, from the console to a stored verdict
Verdict review in the console: clip, evidence
Every verdict keeps the frames that support it and the plan version that produced it.
